experiment.claim: Substantiates spec/target-spec.md's DRAFT "Line regulation" row (< 5 mV/V over 2.97-3.63V, at 1mA and 50mA) against the LDO core-regulation-loop schematic landed by #14 (design/ldo_3v3in_1v8out.sch), using the row's own two named load points and the DRAFT range's own two endpoints. That row is DRAFT (issue #1 not yet ratified) -- the bound below cites it directly, not an invented final limit, and needs re-verification once #1 rules. Each corner runs four discrete .op solves (VIN in {2.97V, 3.63V} x I_LOAD in {1mA, 50mA}, via the deck's own 'alter' on VIN and the load current source, mirroring sim/loop-gain's and sim/iq's multi-point convention), NOT a continuous 'dc vvin ...' sweep -- a continuous sweep over this exact range was tried during this testbench's bring-up and repeatedly hit gmin-stepping/singular-matrix non-convergence partway through (design/README.md's dated 2026-08-25 root-cause section, issue #60 mechanism 4, tracked by #71, already documents this DC-solution-multiplicity behavior for VIN sweeps at 50mA load), taking minutes per corner without completing; four independent .op solves at the range's own endpoints complete in well under a second and reproduce design/README.md's own screening line-regulation numbers (its 'DC operating grid' section also uses discrete VIN points, not a sweep). line_reg_<n>ma_mv_per_v = abs(1000*(vout_hi-vout_lo)/(3.63-2.97)), matching that screening convention. Uses the DR-002 proposed nominal C_out/ESR (1uF/10mOhm), not a window sweep -- same convention as load-transient/dropout-vs-load/psrr-dc. Known risk, not a testbench defect: the same design/README.md section (mechanism 1) documents a thermal-shutdown false-trip at the ff/sf process corners at 125C, independent of load current -- tracked by #69. A corner at that condition is expected to report a non-physical number (pass device driven off), the same documented failure mode the four existing testbenches already show there.
